_comment: Per-chart narratives. CI (build_prompt.py -> GitHub Models -> write_narrative.py) overwrites these from live numbers; this committed copy is the technical fallback so the page always reads well. source = 'fallback' | 'github-models'.

notes.cape: The Shiller CAPE (Cyclically Adjusted Price-to-Earnings) ratio divides the current S&P 500 price by the average inflation-adjusted earnings of the past 10 years, smoothing cyclicality in earnings. As of July 2026, the CAPE stands at 40.47, well above its 140-year average of 17.3 and near the only-ever higher level recorded in December 1999 at 44.19. Historically, CAPE readings above ~39 have presaged negative forward returns: approximately -4% over one year and -20% over two years for the S&P 500. This elevated valuation signals substantial market risk, but timing remains uncertain as the ratio reflects magnitude of potential correction, not precise market inflection points.
notes.buffett: The Buffett Indicator is the ratio of total U.S. stock market capitalization to GDP, serving as a broad valuation gauge. At 231.7% in June 2026, it significantly exceeds previous peaks: 146% at the dot-com top and 110% in 2007. Warren Buffett cautioned that readings above 200% constitute 'playing with fire,' implying stretched valuations relative to economic output that increase vulnerability to sharp corrections. The indicator captures systemic risk by highlighting market valuation divorced from economic fundamentals, but does not predict timing or catalysts for downturns.
notes.concentration: Market concentration measures the weight of top companies within an index, reflecting risk from limited diversification; here, the top 5 S&P 500 stocks comprise ~29.8%, and top 10 stocks 41.0%—up from 17.5% in 2015. The tech sector alone accounts for 48% of the index, indicating sectoral dominance. High concentration can exacerbate volatility and risk if major constituents face valuation shocks or liquidity constraints, impacting the broader market disproportionately. However, concentration effects may persist due to structural trends, complicating signals about market-wide overvaluation.
notes.yieldcurve: The yield curve spread between 10-year and 3-month Treasury yields is 0.69 percentage points as of July 2026. Positive but compressed spreads often portend economic slowing; the New York Fed’s recession probability is currently 31%. The yield curve serves as a forward-looking economic indicator—its shape reflects investor expectations for growth and inflation, with flatter or inverted curves historically preceding recessions and equity corrections. Nonetheless, yield curve signals can vary in lead time and interaction with other factors, so it does not singlehandedly time market downturns.
notes.drypowder: Dry powder refers to cash reserves available for investment; Berkshire Hathaway’s record $397.4 billion in Q1 2026 exemplifies significant latent buying power. Yet 79% of institutions anticipate a decline in dry powder, suggesting expectations of deployment into markets. High levels of dry powder can sustain liquidity and market prices during stress but also imply that sudden shifts in risk appetite could rapidly drain liquidity. The availability of dry powder is thus a key component of the market’s ability to withstand shocks, but its effect depends on investment timing and broader market conditions.
notes.finale: Valuation metrics such as CAPE and Buffett Indicator set the scale or magnitude of potential market corrections, as elevated multiples increase risk of severe drawdowns, but they do not determine timing. Market liquidity functions as the 'music' keeping investors engaged; when liquidity tightens—a common trigger for market corrections—the 'music stops.' The forthcoming IPO lock-up expirations between December 2026 and May 2027, involving companies like SpaceX, OpenAI, and Anthropic, represent a liquidity event that could initiate such a shock. These lock-ups releasing large insider holdings can pressure stock prices and challenge liquidity, potentially ending the current bull market regardless of valuation levels.
